title: The Spout in the Otter Cave
story: In a barnacled sea cave, five otter pups are huddled on a stone ledge, squeaking for help. Hargrelle the Spout Lamprey coils in the pool below, pumping seawater up through her gullet to flood them out. Mr 6 wedges open a clogged barnacle drain with his sword and starts counting — because a knight who knows his rates never panics.
question: The water sits 27 inches below the pups' ledge. Hargrelle's spout raises the water 9 inches every minute, while the opened drain lets 5.4 inches drain away every minute. How many minutes does Mr 6 have before the water reaches the ledge?
solution: Water comes in and goes out, so the real climb each minute is 9 - 5.4 = 3.6 inches.
Mr 6 has 7.5 minutes to carry the pups to safety.
praise: Dividing to find the time was exactly the right instinct — the missing step was subtracting the drain from the spout to get the TRUE rise each minute.
hint: The spout pushes water up and the drain pulls it down. Figure out how much the water really gains in one single minute first.
victory: Mr 6 ferried all five pups out with ninety seconds to spare, then politely plugged Hargrelle's spout with a sea sponge. She burbled, blushed pink, and slithered off to flood somewhere less well-calculated.
imagePrompt: A brave numeral-six knight with a blue cape lifting fuzzy otter pups from a wet stone ledge while a long eel-like lamprey monster spouts seawater below in a glistening barnacle cave lit by shafts of green daylight.
